rationale.overall: B reads as a thick pillowed object the way the REFERENCE slab does, and that volumetric read outweighs its slightly washed body and marginally softer small-size edge.
rationale.material: B's shading wraps around the top-left corner as a curved falloff, matching the REFERENCE's rounded matte body, whereas A applies a straight vertical ramp over a flat card with a hairline rim; A's charcoal values sit closer to the REFERENCE (85→33 vs REF 71→29, B 101→36) but the tone is the smaller error against a missing curvature.
rationale.silhouette: A and B share the same squircle, the same inset dark slab and the same orange window geometry — the pixel diff between them is entirely shading, so there is nothing to separate on outline.
rationale.smallsize: At 32px and 16px A's slab holds a cleaner dark block, while B's soft top rolloff collapses into a mid-grey band that blurs the slab's upper edge.

rationale.overall: The two takes are near-identical apart from the shading of the dark slab, and B's body tone tracks the reference's tonal falloff closely (≈84/53/30 top/mid/bottom against the reference's 76/49/31) where A sits ~18 levels lighter throughout.
rationale.material: B reads as a genuinely dark charcoal slab with a tight top-edge highlight rolling into shadow, matching the reference's volumetric falloff, while A's broader, milkier gradient flattens the form and lifts the mid-body away from the reference's value range.
rationale.silhouette: Both takes share the same outer squircle, inset slab, rule lines and orange aperture — the pixel difference between them is confined entirely to the slab interior, so there is nothing to separate them on shape.
rationale.smallsize: At 128, 32 and 16px the two strips are effectively indistinguishable; B's slightly deeper body gives a hair more separation from the pale bezel, but not enough to call at these sizes.
